items.front: Laws of indices: product, quotient, power-of-power, zero, negative, fractional?
items.examPoint: Laws of indices — product, quotient and power-of-power

items.front: How do you solve an exponential equation like 7^(x−y)=343?
items.back: Write both sides to the same base, then equate the exponents. 343=7³ ⇒ x−y=3.
items.examPoint: Exponential equations — solve for the unknown

items.front: Rationalise 1/(√3−√2); and how to compare surds?
items.back: Multiply by conjugate (√3+√2): denominator = 3−2 = 1 ⇒ √3+√2. Compare surds via a common index = LCM of the roots.

items.front: Log laws: product, quotient, power, change of base?
items.back: log(xy)=log x+log y; log(x/y)=log x−log y; log(xⁿ)=n log x; logₐb=(log꜀b)/(log꜀a).
items.examPoint: Logarithm laws — product, quotient, power and evaluation

items.front: Characteristic & mantissa; digits in a large power?
items.back: Characteristic = integer part = (digits−1); mantissa = positive decimal part. Digits of N = ⌊log₁₀N⌋ + 1.

items.front: HCF & LCM by prime factorization, and the product relation?
items.back: HCF = product of lowest powers of common primes; LCM = highest powers of all primes. For two numbers, A×B = HCF×LCM.
items.examPoint: Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — LCM and HCF

items.back: HCF of fractions = HCF(numerators)/LCM(denominators); LCM of fractions = LCM(numerators)/HCF(denominators).
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — LCM and HCF

items.back: Smallest with common remainder R = LCM+R. Greatest dividing x,y,z with same remainder = HCF of differences. Constant (div−rem)=k ⇒ LCM−k.
items.examPoint: HCF and LCM — remainder and word problems
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — LCM and HCF

items.front: HCF vs LCM: which word problems use which?
items.back: HCF: largest tape/tile, greatest equal distribution, min rows without mixing. LCM: bells/lights coincide, runners meet at start, least common number.
items.examPoint: LCM word problems — bells / lights coinciding
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — LCM and HCF

items.front: Units digit of aⁿ by cyclicity?
items.back: Depends only on base's units digit; reduce exponent mod 4 (remainder 0 = last term). 7→7,9,3,1; 2→2,4,8,6. So 7¹⁰⁵→7.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Cyclicity of Units Digit
